newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Surgutneftegaz sees its 97 oil output flat.
newsitem.headline: Russian Surgutneftegaz sees its 97 oil output flat.

text.p: Russia's third largest oil producer Surgutneftegaz said on Wednesday its 1997 crude oil output would be flat at 32.98 million tonnes (659,600 barrels per day) on the 1996 level of 33.3 million tonnes (666,000 bpd).
A company statement quoted Surgutneftegaz general director Vladimir Bogdanov as saying output stabilisation was crucial to the company's future.

It said the oil producer would carry out intensive work on the Tyansk and Konitlorsk fields, where estimated reserves are in the hundreds of millions of tonnes, and tap a new field, Bittensk. Sixty horizontal wells would be erected at the Fyodorov field.
About 34 percent of the company's wells have a high water content.
Surgutneftegaz said that production at nearly 5,000 wells, with yearly output of about 1.5 million tonnes (30,000 bpd), was not commercially viable even if taxes were to be reduced.
It said high output costs at existing wells had led it to seek new, less costly reserves to tap and that it would increase exploration and drilling.
Exploratory drilling would rise 50 percent on last year's level. Growth in B and C1 reserves would be 16 million tonnes.

Surgutneftegaz is the production unit of the vertically-integrated Surgut Holding. The parent company owns the strategic Kirishi refinery near St Petersburg, a major exporter of refined oil products to northwestern Europe.
